title: \protect Conjecture
body_md:
Let $\alpha,\beta \in \mathbb{R}$ be such that $1,\alpha$ and $\beta$ are linearly independent over $\mathbb{Q}$. Then, for all ${\gamma}, {\delta} \in \mathbb R$,
\[
\liminf_{n \to \infty} n\|n\alpha-{\gamma}\| \cdot \|n\beta-{\delta}\|=0.
\]

title: \protect\remarkname
body_md: This generalises Littlewood's conjecture, since the latter clearly holds when $1, {\alpha}, {\beta}$ are linearly dependent over $\mathbb Q$.

name: OpenAI 2026+, weak inhomogeneous Duffin--Schaeffer conjecture

title: \protect\lemmaname
body_md:
Let $N \in \mathbb{N}$ be large. Then,
for each ${\boldsymbol \ell} \in \mathcal{W}(N)$,
\[
\sum_{n \in B_{{\boldsymbol \ell}}(N)} \frac{\varphi(n)}{n} \gg \frac{N}{p_1^{\ell_1}\cdots p_{k}^{\ell_k}}.
    \]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
With $P := P({\boldsymbol \ell}):= p_1^{\ell_1}\cdots p_k^{\ell_k} \leqslant \sqrt N$, let $n_0 = n_0({\boldsymbol \ell})$ be an integer such that
\[
n_0 \equiv n_j \,\,\mathrm{mod}\,\,p_j^{\ell_j + 1}
\qquad (1 \leqslant j \leqslant k).
\]
This ensures that, for $j=1,2,\ldots,k$,
\[
p_j^{\ell_j} \| (n - n_j)
\quad
\Longleftrightarrow
\quad
p_j^{\ell_j} \| (n - n_0).
\]
Thus, with $q = p_1 \cdots p_k \ll 1$, 
\begin{align*}
\sum_{n \in B_{\boldsymbol \ell}(N)}\frac{\varphi(n)}{n} = \sum_{\substack{ N < n_0 + mP \leqslant 2N
\\(m,q) = 1}} \frac{\varphi(n_0 + mP)}
{n_0 + mP}
= \sum_{\substack{ N < n_0 + mP \leqslant 2N
\\(m,q) = 1}} 
\
\prod_{p \mid (n_0 + mP)} \left(1 - \frac 1 p \right).
\end{align*}
        
                                                                                                                                                  
   
Since $N/P$ is large and $\varphi(q)/q \gg 1$, there are $\gg N/P$ many summands. Hence it suffices, by the AM--GM inequality \cite[Ch. 2]{Ste2004}, to prove that
\begin{equation}
\label{stp}
\prod_{p \leqslant 2N} \left(1 - \frac 1 p \right)^{{\alpha}_p} \gg 1,
\end{equation}
where
\begin{align*}
{\alpha}_p = \frac{P}{N} \# \{ m \in \mathbb Z: (m,q) = 1, \quad p \mid (n_0 + mP) \in (N,2N]
\}.
\end{align*}

Observe that
\[
\prod_{p \leqslant q} \left(1 - \frac 1 p \right)^{{\alpha}_p} \gg 1.
\]
For $p > q$, we have
\[
{\alpha}_p \leqslant \frac{P}{N} \left( \frac{N}{Pp} + 1 \right) \leqslant p^{-1} + N^{-1/2} \ll p^{-1/2}.
\]
Now
\[
-\sum_{p \leqslant 2N} {\alpha}_p \log(1-1/p) \ll \sum_p p^{-3/2} \ll 1,
\]
which delivers \eqref{stp} and completes the proof of the lemma.

title: \protect Conjecture
body_md:
Let ${\alpha} \in \mathbb R$ be irrational, and let $\mathcal D = (d_\ell)_{\ell = 1}^\infty$ be an increasing sequence of positive integers such that $d_\ell \mid d_{\ell + 1}$ for all $\ell$. Then, for all $n_0 \in \mathbb Z$ and all ${\gamma} \in \mathbb R$,
\[
\liminf_{n \to \infty} n 
| n - n_0|_\mathcal D 
\| n {\alpha} - {\gamma} \| = 0.
\]
head: environment
name: Mixed inhomogeneous Littlewood

label: MIG
title: \protect Conjecture
body_md:
\label{MIG}
Let $\mathcal D =(d_\ell)_{\ell = 1}^\infty$ be an increasing  sequence of positive integers such that $d_\ell \mid d_{\ell+1}$ for all $\ell$. Let $n_0 \in \mathbb Z$ and ${\gamma} \in \mathbb R$, and let $\psi: \mathbb N \to [0, \infty)$ be a non-increasing function such that
\[
\sum_{n=1}^\infty
\psi(n) \max \{ k: d_k \leqslant n \}
= \infty.
\]
Then, for almost all ${\alpha} \in \mathbb R$, there exist infinitely many $n \in \mathbb N$ such that
\[
|n - n_0|_\mathcal D \| n {\alpha} - {\gamma} \| < \psi(n).
\]
head: environment
name: Mixed inhomogeneous Gallagher

title: \protect\theoremname
body_md:
Let $\mathcal D = (d_\ell)_{\ell = 1}^\infty$ be an increasing sequence of positive integers such that $d_\ell \mid d_{\ell+1}$ for all $\ell$ and, for all $L \in \mathbb N$,
\[
\sum_{\ell \leqslant L} \frac{\varphi(d_\ell)}{d_\ell} \gg L.
\]
Let ${\gamma} \in \mathbb R$, and let $\psi: \mathbb N \to [0, \infty)$ be a non-increasing function such that 
\[
\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\psi(n) \max \{ k: d_k \leqslant n \} = \infty.
\]
Then, for almost all ${\alpha} \in \mathbb R$, there exist infinitely many $n \in \mathbb N$ such that
\[
|n |_\mathcal D \| n {\alpha} - {\gamma} \| < \psi(n).
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $N \in \mathbb N$ be large in terms of the sequence $\mathcal D$, and let $L \in \mathbb N$ be maximal such that $d_L \leqslant 2N$. Then $L$ is also large.
Define, for $\ell \in \mathbb N$,
\[
\mathcal B_\ell(N) = \{ n \in \mathbb Z: N < n \leqslant 2N, \quad
d_\ell \mid n, \quad d_{\ell + 1} \nmid n \}.
\]
Note that if $\ell \leqslant L/2$ then
\[
\frac{2N}{d_{\ell+1}} \geqslant
\frac{d_L}{d_{\ell+1}} \geqslant 2^{L - \ell - 1} \geqslant 2^{(L-2)/2} \geqslant 100.
\]
We claim that, for each $\ell \leqslant L/2$,
\[
\sum_{n \in \mathcal B_\ell (N)} \frac{\varphi(n)}{n} \gg
\frac{\varphi(d_\ell) N}{d_\ell^2}.
\]

To prove the claim, we use the fact that $\varphi(xy) \geqslant \varphi(x) \varphi(y)$ for all $x, y \in \mathbb N$. Writing $r_\ell = d_{\ell+1}/d_\ell$,
\begin{align*}
\sum_{n \in \mathcal B_\ell (N)} \frac{\varphi(n)}{n} \geqslant \frac{\varphi(d_\ell)}{d_\ell}
\
\sum_{\substack{N/d_\ell < m \leqslant 2N/d_\ell \\ r_\ell \nmid m}} \frac{\varphi(m)}{m}.
\end{align*}
There are $\gg N/d_\ell$ many summands so, by the AM--GM inequality, it suffices for the claim to prove that
\begin{equation}
\label{stp2}
\prod_{p} \left(1 - \frac1p \right)^{{\alpha}_p} \gg 1,
\end{equation}
where now we define
\[
{\alpha}_p = \frac{d_\ell}{N}
\# \{ m \in \mathbb Z: r_{\ell} \nmid m,
\ p \mid m \in (N/d_\ell, 2N/d_\ell] \}.
\]
Since 
\[
{\alpha}_p \leqslant \frac{d_\ell}{N}
\# \{ m \in \mathbb Z:
p \mid m \in [1, 2N/d_\ell] \}
\leqslant 2/p
\]
for all primes $p$, we have
\[
- \sum_p {\alpha}_p \log(1- 1/p) \ll \sum_p p^{-2} \ll 1,
\]
which furnishes \eqref{stp2} and with it the claim.

With the claim at hand, we compute that
\begin{align}
\notag
\sum_{N < n \leqslant 2N} \frac{\varphi(n) \psi(n)}{n | n |_\mathcal D} &\geqslant \sum_{\ell \leqslant L/2} \
d_\ell \psi(2N)
\sum_{n \in \mathcal B_\ell(N)} 
\frac{\varphi(n)}{n} \\
\label{KeyAvg}
&\gg N \psi(2N) \sum_{\ell \leqslant L/2} \frac{\varphi(d_\ell)}{d_\ell} \gg N \psi(2N)L.
\end{align}
By the Cauchy condensation test,
\[
\sum_{m=1}^\infty 2^m \psi(2^m)  \max \{ k: d_k \leqslant 2^m \} = \infty.
\]
In particular, by summing \eqref{KeyAvg} over large $N = 2^{m-1}$, we find
\[
\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{\varphi(n) \psi(n)}{n | n |_\mathcal D} = \infty.
\]
The desired conclusion now follows upon applying Theorem \ref{WeakInhomDuff}.
